title: Mascarpone Ice Cream (No Egg)
changes_from_base: Mascarpone and a little brown sugar replace the strawberries; the cream is cut back and the milk raised to keep the base scoopable.
summary: A rich, egg-free ice cream built on cold mascarpone, with a touch of brown sugar for warmth. It tastes like the creamy part of tiramisu, dense and smooth.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Sweet milk
steps.text: Warm the milk, both sugars, the syrup and the salt in the saucepan over medium heat, stirring, just until the sugar has dissolved and the milk steams. Pour into the jug and cool completely.

steps.title: Loosen the mascarpone
steps.text: In the large bowl, whisk the cold mascarpone with about a third of the cream until smooth and free of lumps, then whisk in the rest of the cream and the vanilla.

steps.title: Combine and chill
steps.text: Whisk the cooled milk into the mascarpone cream a little at a time so it stays silky, then cover and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn for 20-25 min, until it looks like thick soft serve. Mascarpone churns faster than plain cream, so check it early.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Scrape into the container, press baking paper on the surface and freeze for at least 4 h. Give it 10 min out of the freezer before scooping.

tips: Keep the mascarpone cold and loosen it with a little cream first, or it can turn grainy.
Use mascarpone made with microbial rennet or acid-set (check the label).
Serve with crushed amaretti or a drizzle of strong coffee.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper pressed on the surface in the freezer for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10 min in the fridge before scooping.
